name: Versant Media Group, Inc.

profile.description: Versant Media Group is an independent media company spun off from Comcast on January 2, 2026, trading on Nasdaq since January 5, 2026. The company operates a portfolio of cable television networks including USA Network, Bravo, CNBC, MSNBC, E!, Syfy, Oxygen, and Golf Channel, along with digital platforms Fandango and GolfNow. Revenue is derived from linear distribution (pay-TV affiliate fees), advertising, and platform services. Full-year 2025 revenue of $6.69 billion with $2.42 billion adjusted EBITDA.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Versant inherited mature cable assets from Comcast/NBCUniversal with no transformative product launches as an independent entity — Fandango integration and GolfNow expansion represent incremental digital extensions, not business model innovation [1][4]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products shipping to customers and no quantified AI-driven efficiencies reported; board member David Eun brings AI expertise from Samsung NEXT but no commercial AI products are in market [4]. Market Share (1/2): Versant operates established cable network brands (USA, Bravo, CNBC, MSNBC) with meaningful audience share, but is a declining participant as cord-cutting erodes linear TV viewership — linear distribution revenue fell 7% in Q1 2026 to $1.01B [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): Management has discussed plans to diversify beyond cable TV through acquisitions and new revenue streams, but no specific next-generation products have been named with firm timelines or revenue visibility [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No disclosed R&D spending as a percentage of revenue; the company operates media networks rather than a technology platform.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Versant describes itself as having 'an experienced leadership team with a proven track record, deep industry expertise and a forward-thinking approach' — generic corporate language interchangeable with any media company, with no distinctive purpose or vision beyond managing legacy cable assets [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of foundation, charitable programs, or community investment initiatives found for Versant as a standalone entity in its first six months of independence. Employee Retention (0/2): No employee tenure or turnover data available for this newly independent company; the spinoff process itself creates organizational uncertainty as employees transition from Comcast. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful insider buying data available; the company began trading only six months ago and no net insider purchases have been reported.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Versant's standout financial strength is its extremely low valuation — forward P/E of 5.71 and trailing P/E of 6.09 reflect deep market skepticism about cable TV's structural future [5]. Debt-to-equity of 9% ($983M debt, $55M cash) provides unusual balance sheet flexibility for a media spinoff [2]. However, ROE of only 8.73% signals mediocre capital efficiency, and profit margin of 13.91% is below the 20% target. Revenue declined 5.3% in full-year 2025 to $6.69B with net income down 31.8% to $930M, driven by secular cord-cutting headwinds, though Q1 2026 showed improvement with only a 1% revenue decline and 5% EBITDA growth [1][2]. Free cash flow of $1.86B TTM ($558M in Q1 alone) supports the $0.375 quarterly dividend and $1B share buyback authorization.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Versant's cable TV networks face moderate AI exposure — live sports (Golf Channel, NBC Sports) and breaking news programming (CNBC, MSNBC) are structurally protected from AI substitution, as audiences demand real-time, human-anchored coverage that AI cannot replicate [4]. However, scripted and unscripted entertainment content (Bravo, USA, Syfy, E!) faces potential AI disruption as generative AI tools reduce production costs for competitors and shift audience attention to AI-curated platforms. Advertising revenue ($368M Q1, down 5%) could face compression as AI-powered programmatic platforms reduce the premium cable TV commands over digital alternatives [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-powered products or services generating meaningful revenue; while the company has AI-experienced board members, no AI features have shipped or AI-driven efficiencies been reported [4].

infinite_game.summary: Versant was created as a financial separation vehicle to house Comcast's declining cable TV assets, not as a company born from a Just Cause or vision of a better future. The spinoff structure itself reveals finite game thinking — Comcast retained the growing Peacock streaming platform while spinning off the shrinking linear TV business. Sinek would view this as a company organized around extracting remaining value from a declining business model rather than playing to keep playing.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): Versant has no articulated Just Cause. The company was created through a corporate spinoff to separate declining cable assets from Comcast's growth businesses — there is no vision of a future state that inspires sacrifice or long-term commitment [3][4]. The implicit purpose is to manage the decline of linear TV while maximizing cash extraction. Sinek would categorize this as a textbook finite player: the company exists because of a financial transaction, not because of a cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Mark Lazarus and the leadership team bring decades of media industry experience from Comcast/NBCUniversal, providing organizational stability during the transition to independence [3]. The board includes David Novak (former YUM! Brands CEO) and other experienced directors spanning entertainment, technology, and finance. However, as a newly independent company with inherited employees who joined Comcast rather than Versant, there is no evidence yet of whether the company fosters psychological safety or empowerment independent of Comcast's corporate umbrella.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of an infinite competitive mindset. Versant's competitive positioning focuses on 'trusted brands' and 'forward-thinking approach' but lacks acknowledgment of competitors' strengths or evidence that competitive pressure is used for self-improvement [3][4]. The strategic narrative is defensive — protecting legacy positions against cord-cutting — rather than using streaming rivals' strengths to inform its own evolution.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): Versant has existed as an independent entity for only six months and has not demonstrated any strategic flexibility. The company inherited a legacy cable TV business model and has stated intentions to diversify through acquisitions, but no transformative pivot has been executed or announced with specificity [4]. The company is structurally tied to its founding business model and too young to have been tested on existential flexibility.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of courageous leadership decisions. Versant's creation was driven by Comcast's strategic decision to separate declining assets, not by Versant leadership's visionary initiative. The $1B share buyback authorization and $0.375 quarterly dividend are standard capital return programs, not courageous bets on the future [1]. No examples of sacrificing near-term results for long-term capability building have emerged in the company's brief independent history.

investment_thesis: Versant Media trades at a deeply discounted 5.71x forward P/E with a 4.13% dividend yield, $1B buyback authorization, and $2.42B adjusted EBITDA on $6.69B revenue — offering compelling near-term cash returns for income-oriented investors [1][2]. Q1 2026 showed margin resilience with adjusted EBITDA up 5% YoY to $704M despite a 1% revenue decline, and free cash flow of $558M in a single quarter demonstrates exceptional cash generation. Platforms revenue (GolfNow, Fandango) grew 9% to $192M, suggesting digital diversification is gaining early traction [1]. At a $5.14B market cap with $1.86B annual FCF, the stock offers a 36% free cash flow yield.
thesis_continued: The bear case is structural and powerful: linear TV distribution revenue ($1.01B in Q1, down 7%) represents approximately 60% of total revenue and is in secular decline as cord-cutting accelerates with no floor in sight — pay-TV subscribers have fallen from over 100M to approximately 60M over the past decade [1][4]. Versant was deliberately created as a spinoff of Comcast's declining assets while Comcast retained the growing Peacock streaming platform, signaling that even the parent company viewed these properties as ex-growth. Full-year 2025 net income fell 31.8% to $930M despite only a 5.3% revenue decline, revealing operating leverage that works in both directions [2]. Without a credible path to replace declining linear revenue through digital transformation, the low multiple may be a value trap rather than a buying opportunity — the company lacks the innovation, mission, and long-term strategic vision that the IOWN framework values most highly.
key_catalysts: Platforms segment (GolfNow, Fandango) growing 9% YoY to $192M in Q1 2026 represents an emerging diversification engine if management can accelerate digital revenue through acquisitions and organic investment [1]
FCF yield of approximately 36% ($1.86B FCF on $5.14B market cap) supports aggressive capital return through the $1B buyback and 4.13% dividend yield, providing downside support [1][2]
Advertising revenue decline improving from -12% in prior year to -5% in Q1 2026, suggesting potential stabilization as new measurement tools and digital ad formats gain traction [1]
key_risks: Linear distribution revenue declining 7% YoY in Q1 2026 with no structural floor — continued cord-cutting could accelerate if economic conditions weaken, threatening the 60% of revenue derived from pay-TV affiliate fees [1]

Versant was created through a spinoff precisely because Comcast wanted to separate itself from these declining assets — structural headwinds are baked into the company's DNA and will persist regardless of management execution [4]
Full-year 2025 net income declined 31.8% on only a 5.3% revenue decline, demonstrating negative operating leverage that could compress earnings dramatically if revenue declines accelerate [2]
